All are time-critical; the plan instead contains warm leads at 75-105% of threshold.

R1, R2, R4 and R6 produced zero actions: workflow_drift contains only categorization_miss (5) and stale_approaching (34). No meeting_no_followup, followup_not_fired, untagged_in_queue or abandonment_next findings were emitted, so four of six rules were untested by this day.

CONTRACT DISAGREEMENT (criterion 2) -- both planner-agent.md and plan-schema.md state pct_of_threshold is emitted at extensions.ghl.workflow_drift[].pct_of_threshold. It is not. workflow_drift entries carry type, contact, detail, ref, severity and days_overdue only. The numeric pct_of_threshold lives in extensions.ghl.opportunities[], joined on workflow_drift[].ref == opportunities[].opportunity_id; that join is what produced every rank here. It was also cross-checked against the identity pct = (days_overdue + stale_threshold_days) / stale_threshold_days, which held exactly on every finding tested. No percentage was parsed from detail prose.

CONTRACT DISAGREEMENT (criterion 2) -- workflow_drift entries carry no contact_id. entity.ghl_contact_id was resolved for every action via the same opportunities[] join, or from the contact-detail URL in the matching items[] entry. Contract requires source IDs whenever the finding has one, but the finding record itself does not.

CONTRACT DISAGREEMENT (criterion 2) -- the Ranking tie-break names first_contact. No such field exists anywhere in the ingest output. Ties at 157% (ranks 13-14), 130% (16-17) and 105% (22-25) were broken by workflow_drift emission order instead. No tie straddles the 25-action cap, so this did not change which actions were planned today, but the rule is not implementable as written.

CONTRACT DISAGREEMENT (criterion 2) -- action ids are not hashes. The schema requires a hash of (entity source ID + rule_id + finding id), but the planner's tools grant is Read and Write only, with no hashing primitive available. ids here are the deterministic composite plan-<rule_id>-<opportunity_id>, which preserves the stability property the hash exists to guarantee (same finding, same id, across re-runs) without fabricating hex that no implementation could reproduce. Resolve before any approvals file is ever written against these ids.

TRACEABILITY -- only 10 of the 34 stale_approaching findings appear as itemized entries in items[]; the other 24 are covered by the rollup ghl-rollup-2026-09-08 and exist only in extensions.ghl.workflow_drift. basis.item_id for those was constructed as ghl-drift-stale_approaching-<ref>, matching the id convention ghl-ingest-agent uses for the ones it did itemize. Confirm that convention is stable before a consumer joins on it.

R3 tier gating did not bind on any finding. ghl-ingest-agent emits stale_approaching only at 75% of threshold or above, and the lowest finding today is exactly 75%, so all 34 cleared their tier (hot any, warm 60%, untagged/unqualified 70%). No cold-tagged findings exist at all -- 107 were excluded upstream by the 0b. Far Out (Cold) + lead: cold rule -- so the 80% cold tier was never exercised.
